When Sparks Fly (2014) In 2014, Meghan finally landed her first major film role in Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly Meghan's character Amy finds there's no place like how when she reunited with her high school sweetheart In 2014, Meghan finally landed a major film role, playing the lead role in the Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly. She played Amy Peterson, a journalist who quits her small town for the big city of Chicago. She then returned to her hometown to write a human interest story about Independence Day weekend. Amy discovered that there's no place like home - and no boy like her high school sweetheart. Meghan said at the time: 'I wanted to do a romantic comedy. When the script came in, it was exactly the kind of project I wanted to be part of. 'It was light and easy and it was a departure from Rachel [Suits], who is so refined and polished. Amy Peterson is very opposite and closer to my true personality. 'It was fun to eat ribs and get barbecue sauce all over my face and run around in jeans all day.' Hallmark films all generally follow the same plot points, and while they make for comforting watching, are generally not considered 'challenging' acting roles. In 2021 alone, the channel made 41 Christmas films, with each film relatively low budget and without famous names. Anti-Social (2015) Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin) in Anti-Social Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role Set in England and filmed largely in Hungary, Anti-Social followed a successful street artist who was forced to jeopardise his future to help his criminal brother when gang rivalry escalates. The gangland war turned their lives upside down, bringing the attention of the police as well as other criminals. The low-budget British coming-of-age story was inspired by a number of real-life smash-and-grab raids across London from 2009 to 2013. Again, the Duchess was chosen to play the female lead and it even co-starred grime star Skepta. Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin), a talented Banksy-esque street-artist who was sucked into crime. One of her lines included: 'I know you have had to climb a mountain to get away from this crap and see life for what it can be. You inspire me.' Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role as bosses sought to capitalise on her new royal links. Originally, it had been shown at just 40 screens in the UK when it was released in 2015. Speaking of the decision to re-release it, Director Reg Traviss - who had dated Amy Winehouse before she died - said he wanted to 'delve deeper into one of the storylines with.. a shorter, more compact version of the original'. In the three-minute trailer, Meghan's character was shown modelling perfume, emerging from a shower and drinking champagne at a number of West End nightclubs. She was heard saying: 'I'm going to go and see my boyfriend, he's an artist. A street artist.' In a scene which showed shoot-outs in London, depicting Marcus and his cool friends getting pulled into a dangerous gang war, she said: 'I hate violence... I'm from a sleepy little beach town, I'm just not used to this.' Upon its release, the film generally received negative reviews, with one critic calling the film a 'painful slog'. In The Observer, critic Mark Kermode awarded it two stars, calling it an 'uninspiring crime caper' that 'sits awkwardly alongside dreary discussions of the politics of street art'. Dater's Handbook (2016) Meghan's final film role saw her play Cassandra Barber in 2016's Dater's Handbook Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams In Meghan's final film role before quitting the industry upon joining the Royal Family, she played another lead role for the Hallmark Channel, in 2016's Dater's Handbook. The romantic movie centred around Cassandra Barber, who realised she had a recurring habit of picking the wrong type of guy, turning to relationship expert, Dr. Susie, and her latest self-help book, The Dater's Handbook to help with her ailing love life. 'Of course I wanna get married,' Meghan's character Cass told her mother. 'I've got to change how I choose relationships.' She followed the advice in Dr. Susie's book to evaluate potential suitors, and was forced to choose between reliable George (Jonathan Scarfe) and fun-loving Robert (Kristoffer Polaha). Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams. Little did Meghan know that six months later she'd meet her real-life prince. Successful career women, both Cassandra and Meghan were set up with their dream suitor by a mutual pal, bonding on and off-screen with their respective suitors over their shared love of animals and the great outdoors. Additionally, Meghan and her character were whisked away on sporty dates by their suitors - while Cass' mother joined the pair at a concert in the movie, Harry flew Meghan's mother Doria to the Invictus Games in Toronto in real life. Many joked at the time of the movie's release that while the character she played on screen had been unlucky in love, Meghan's real love life was very different. During the film's press tour, Meghan said: 'At the end of the day, when it comes down to finding the person that you're right for, that's not the person you're going to play games with. 'I think following her heart has really ended up proving to work out well for Cass, and I think for a lot of women watching this, I would give them that same advice.' The film, a classic Hallmark movie, was branded 'predictable and simple' by critics. On IMDB, one reviewer even said: 'The story was silly, the acting was below average, and the actors had no chemistry.' Credit: The CW When it comes to satisfying our television cravings, nothing works better than a piping hot serve of nostalgia. If you find yourself picking up that handy-dandy TV remote in search of some \'00s classics , you can hardly be blamed for yearning for an incredible (if somewhat cringeworthy) era gone by. We all occasionally long for the days when boy bands ruled the world, Britney Spears was our every ringtone, and being on-trend meant wearing low-rise denim while texting with a T-Mobile Sidekick. The \'00s gave us classic comedies, like The Office and Arrested Development , copious iconic reality shows (who could ever forget Rock of Love ?), dozens of comforting favorites ( Rules of Engagement , we hardly knew ye), and more. With this much greatness packed into one decade, it can be hard to decide what to binge, so we rounded up some of the best 2000s TV shows that you should rewatch, like, immediately. The Best 2000s Comedy TV Shows \'30 Rock\' (2006–2013) Credit: Courtesy Starring: Tina Fey , Alec Baldwin, Tracy Morgan, Jane Krakowski, and Jack McBrayer Advertisement Advertisement Why it makes the list: Thanks to Fey\'s history with NBC and Saturday Night Live , this show about working in the entertainment industry has a certain je ne sais quoi. The jokes are fired off at a mile per minute, but each one is well-earned; you\'ll be cracking up for your entire binge. WATCH NOW \'Arrested Development\' (2003–2006, 2013, 2018–2019) Credit: Fox Starring: Jason Bateman, Michael Cera , Portia de Rossi, Will Arnett, Alia Shawkat, and Tony Hale Why it makes the list: Dysfunctional families who go from filthy, stinking rich to dirt poor in hours are just the kind we love to see in our fave comedies—Just ask those who were inspired by Arrested Development (ahem, Schitt\'s Creek ) . Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW \'Desperate Housewives\' (2004–2012) Credit: ABC Starring: Teri Hatcher, Felicity Huffman, Marcia Cross, Eva Longoria, Jesse Metcalfe, and James Denton Why it makes the list: Suburban life suddenly didn\'t seem all that boring once we had been introduced to the ladies of Wisteria Lane. From hooking up with the sons of their neighbors to revenge plots gone off the rails, every episode was a totally not normal day in the neighborhood. WATCH NOW \'Entourage\' (2004–2011) Credit: HBO Starring: Adrian Grenier, Kevin Dillon, Kevin Connolly, and Jerry Ferrara Why it makes the list: Sex and the City wasn’t HBO’s only mid-’00s smash: Entourage , the series loosely based on Mark Wahlberg’s life in Hollywood with his best buds, was pulling in two to three million viewers per episode at the height of its 2000s fame. Between the glitzy parties, the wheelings and dealings, and the copious auditions, it gave viewers a rare peek behind the Hollywood—and it proved to be irresistible. Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW \'Everybody Hates Chris\' (2005–2009) Credit: UPN/The CW Starring: Terry Crews, Tyler James Williams, Tichina Arnold, Tequan Richmond, Imani Hakim, and Vincent Martella Why it makes the list: Comedian Chris Rock narrates this iconic Black TV show about his childhood in the \'80s. His clever and honest retelling is so good, it won an NAACP Image Award for writing in 2007. WATCH NOW \'Girlfriends\' (2000–2008) Credit: UPN/The CW Starring: Tracee Ellis Ross , Golden Brooks, Persia White, Reginald C. Hayes, and Jill Marie Jones Why it makes the list: There are tons of shows about groups of 20-somethings going through life together, but if you ask us, none are quite as funny or relatable as Girlfriends . Tackling issues from interracial relationships to parenthood, the show that introduced us to Tracee Ellis Ross is a must-watch. Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW \'How I Met Your Mother\' (2005–2014) Credit: CBS Starring: Josh Radnor, Jason Segel, Cobie Smulders, Neil Patrick Harris, and Alyson Hannigan Why it makes the list: Hearing how one\'s parents met shouldn\'t be this funny. Years later, we haven\'t stopped quoting the series (or shaking our heads over that massively divisive finale). WATCH NOW \'The Office\' (2005–2013) Credit: Courtesy Starring: Steve Carell, Jenna Fischer, John Krasinski, Mindy Kaling, B.J. Novak, Angela Kinsey, and Ed Helms Why it makes the list: Friends was to the \'90s what The Office was to the \'00s. The documentary-style series about a dysfunctional paper company and its Scranton, Pennsylvania employees brought a whole new outlook to the 9-to-5 experience. Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW \'Reba\' (2001–2007) Credit: The WB Starring: Reba McEntire, JoAnna Garcia Swisher, Steve Howey, Christopher Rich, and Melissa Peterman Why it makes the list: Reba \'s main character stood out from the \'00s sitcom pack as a single mother of three. Rather than a "woe-is-me" storyline, however, the country singer/actress managed to navigate every situation with strength and her trademark Southern sass. WATCH NOW \'Rules of Engagement\' (2007–2013) Credit: CBS Starring: David Spade, Megyn Price, Bianca Kajlich, Patrick Warburton, Oliver Hudson, and Adhir Kalyan Why it makes the list: Six friends who live in close vicinity and regularly meet up at a cafe may sound familiar, but there are a few key differences between Friends and Rules of Engagement . David Spade’s lovably slimy character of Russell is far more crude than Joey (Matthew LeBlanc would never), and the couples are more clearly cemented than they were in Friends. But like its forebearer, you\'ll be laughing the whole way through as their romantic dynamics shift over 100 episodes. Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW \'Scrubs\' (2001–2010) Credit: NBC Starring: Zach Braff, Donald Faison, Sarah Chalke, John C. McGinley, Ken Jenkins, and Neil Flynn Why it makes the list: Scrubs singlehandedly proved that hospital-based shows could be fun. Unlike the usual high-drama fests the genre is known for (we still love you, Grey\'s Anatomy !), this one\'s a barrel of laughs. WATCH NOW \'Sex and the City\' (1998–2004) Credit: HBO Starring: Sarah Jessica Parker , Kim Cattrall , Kristin Davis, and Cynthia Nixon Why it makes the list: It may have started at the tail end of the ‘90s, but when you think of the early aughts, Sex and the City , there\'s no doubt that the show\'s fashion moments come to mind. And more than two decades after its release (plus two movies, a prequel series, and, of course, the reboot series And Just Like That… ), its characters are still some of the most beloved of our time. Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW \'Ugly Betty\' (2006–2010) Credit: ABC Starring: America Ferrera , Ana Ortiz, Mark Indelicato, Eric Mabius, Tony Plana, Ashley Jensen, and Vanessa Williams Why it makes the list: You can\'t help but love Betty Suarez (Ferrera) in this workplace comedy—even if she does wear a kitschy poncho to her first day on the job at the prestigious Mode magazine. Its heartwarming heroine even made history, with Ferrera becoming the first Latina to win the Best Actress in a Comedy Series Emmy for her role. WATCH NOW \'What I Like About You\' (2002–2006) Credit: The WB Starring: Amanda Bynes, Jennie Garth, Wesley Jonathan, Leslie Grossman, Allison Munn, and Nick Zano Why it makes the list: Would it even be a 2000s list without an appearance from teen queen Amanda Bynes? While iconic 2000s movies like What a Girl Wants and She\'s the Man get all the love, this underrated favorite about a 16-year-old who moves in with her older sister (Garth) has all her usual charm—and more. Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW The Best 2000s Dramas \'Big Love\' (2006–2011) Credit: Alamy Starring: Bill Paxton, Jeanne Tripplehorn, Chloë Sevigny, Ginnifer Goodwin, and Amanda Seyfried Why it makes the list: This drama series about a fundamentalist Mormon man and his three wives was a huge late-aughts hit for HBO. The acting was especially admired, with several cast members earning Emmy and Golden Globe nods (Sevigny took home a win for the latter) throughout its five-season run. WATCH NOW \'Breaking Bad\' (2008–2013) Credit: Alamy Starring: Bryan Cranston, Aaron Paul, Anna Gunn, Betsy Brandt, RJ Mitte, and Dean Norris Why it makes the list: When it comes to antiheroes, none compare to high school teacher-turned-methamphetamine seller Walter White (Bryan Cranston). While his heart starts in the right place—he longs to secure a stable financial future for his family before he dies from stage-three lung cancer—the lines between right and wrong get blurry, fast. Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW \'The L Word\' (2004–2009) Credit: Alamy Starring: Jennifer Beals, Mia Kirshner, Pam Grier, Laurel Holloman, and Katherine Moennig Why it makes the list: This Showtime series broke new ground with a cast made up completely of lesbian and bisexual female characters . While there are some problematic elements by 2020s standards, it still serves as a largely true snapshot of what life was like for many queer women in the 2000s. WATCH NOW \'Lost\' (2004–2010) Credit: ABC Starring: Matthew Fox, Naveen Andrews, Jorge Garcia, Josh Holloway, Yunjin Kim, Evangeline Lilly, Emilie de Ravin, and Daniel Dae Kim Why it makes the list: Theoretically, watching a group of strangers trying to survive on a deserted island after a deadly plane crash should get boring after a couple of seasons, but with legendary showrunner J.J. Abrams at the helm of Lost , we say, "Think again." Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW \'Prison Break\' (2005–2009; 2017) Credit: Fox Starring: Wentworth Miller, Dominic Purcell, Sarah Wayne Callies, Robert Knepper, and Amaury Nolasco Why it makes the list: Prison Break is so good, fans can’t let it go. In 2017, eight years after it originally went off the air, the original cast was brought back for a fifth season. Eight years after that , Hulu announced a reboot of the show featuring an all-new cast. It’s about a man (Wentworth Miller) who intentionally gets sent to a high-security prison to help his brother escape before his scheduled execution—and needless to say, it’s utterly gripping. WATCH NOW \'Six Feet Under\' (2001–2005) Credit: HBO Starring: Peter Krause, Michael C. Hall, Frances Conroy, Lauren Ambrose, and Freddy Rodriguez Advertisement Advertisement Why it makes the list: If you haven\'t gathered by now, HBO was in its heyday in the early aughts, and Six Feet Under is one of the series that contributed to that reputation. While it might not get as much love as some of the network\'s other hits, the the Fishers and their family-owned funeral home definitely makes for some binge-worthy subject matter. WATCH NOW \'The Sopranos\' (1999–2007) Credit: Digital Spy Starring: James Gandolfini, Lorraine Bracco, Edie Falco, Michael Imperioli, and Steven Van Zandt Why it makes the list: Before Games of Thrones became the hot girl on campus (a.k.a HBO ) The Sopranos ruled the network. In fact, we\'d go so far as to say that this show about a mob boss and his family set the \'00s standard for dramedies everywhere. (It\'s also a #mobwifeaesthetic treasure trove.) Advertisement Advertisement WATCH NOW \'Weeds\' (2005–2012) Credit: Alamy Starring: Mary-Louise Parker, Mary-Kate Olsen, Elizabeth Perkins, Justin Kirk, Tonye Patano, and Romany Malco Why it makes the list: There was no shortage of dark dramedies on premium cable in the 2000s, but only one was powerful enough to lure Mary-Kate Olsen to the small screen. This Showtime offering followed a suburban single mother (Parker) through her decision to start selling marijuana to support her family’s upper-middle-class lifestyle after the untimely death of her husband. WATCH NOW \'The West Wing\' (1999–2006) Credit: NBC Starring: Martin Sheen, Rob Lowe, Allison Janney, John Spencer, and Bradley Whitford Why it makes the list: A fair share of political dramas center around the White House, and we owe them all to this bad boy right here. Countless scandals, threats, and political scuffles ran amok over the series\' seven seasons, and the show introduced us to a ton of stars we still love today. WATCH NOW \'The Wire\' (2002–2008) Credit: HBO Starring: Dominic West, Wendell Pierce, Lance Reddick, Sonja Sohn, John Doman, and Deirdre Lovejoy Why it makes the list: Every part of the drug food chain, from addicts and dealers to cops and politicians, gets dissected in this gritty HBO drama set in Baltimore. Narcos , who? WATCH NOW The Best 2000s Mystery TV Shows \'Alias\' (2001–2006) Credit: Alamy Starring: Jennifer Garner , Ron Rifkin, Carl Lumbly, Kevin Weisman, and Victor Garber Why it makes the list: Watching a fresh-faced Garner kick some ass for a secret branch of the CIA is just what the doctor ordered! Also, a young Bradley Cooper appears in several episodes, so our complaints are minimal. WATCH NOW \'The Closer\' (2005–2012) Credit: Alamy/AJ Pics Starring: Kyra Sedgwick, J. K. Simmons, Corey Reynolds, Robert Gossett, G.W. Bailey, and Tony Denison Why it makes the list: Everyone loves a gripping crime show , and The Closer gives the genre a good dose of girl power. LAPD Deputy Chief Brenda Leigh Johnson (Sedgwick) is smart, tough, and hellbent on getting her man—even if it means breaking a rule of her own to get the job done. Basically? She’s a total boss. WATCH NOW \'Dexter\' (2006–2013) Credit: Alamy Starring: Michael C. Hall, Julie Benz, Jennifer Carpenter, Erik King, and Lauren Vélez Why it makes the list: Dexter put a fresh spin on the classic whodunnit by making its titular forensic analyst a vigilante serial killer by night. The series remained so popular that it spawned a follow-up limited series in 2021 and a prequel series that debuted in late 2024. WATCH NOW \'Ghost Whisperer\' 2005–2012) Credit: CBS Starring: Jennifer Love Hewitt , David Conrad, Camryn Manheim, Jamie Kennedy, Aisha Tyler, and Jay Mohr Why it makes the list: Between her movies, music videos (we’ll never get LFO’s “Girl on TV” out of our heads!), and her iconic Neutrogena commercials, Jennifer Love Hewitt was seemingly never in one spot for too long in the late ‘90s. By the time the mid-2000s rolled around, however, fans could count on seeing her every week as Melinda Gordon on Ghost Whisperer . Her character pulled double-duty as an antique shop owner and paranormal communicator with a side hustle involving helping countless trapped souls set their spirits at ease over the course of the show’s seven-year run. WATCH NOW \'Monk\' (2002–2009) Credit: Alamy Starring: Tony Shalhoub, Bitty Schram, Jason Gray-Stanford, Ted Levine, and Traylor Howard Why it makes the list: Another still-beloved gem, Monk centers on Adrian Monk (Tony Shaloub), a titular detective who must grapple with obsessive-compulsive disorder, germophobia, and a host of other mental health issues while simultaneously solving various mysteries and solving his wife’s cold case murder. Fun fact: Monk ’s 2009 finale once held the record for the most-watched scripted cable drama. (It was later overtaken by zombies with an episode of The Walking Dead. ) WATCH NOW \'Veronica Mars\' (2004–2007; 2019) Credit: Alamy Starring: Kristen Bell , Percy Daggs III, Teddy Dunn, Jason Dohring, and Enrico Colantoni Why it makes the list: Bell plays the titular detective in this mid-aughts show, which blended teen drama and crime into one extra-sharp and smartly written series. Fans loved it so much that they crowdfunded a movie version in 2014, which in turn inspired Hulu to take up the mantle and put out a belated fourth season of the show in 2019. WATCH NOW The Best 2000s Reality TV Shows \'America’s Next Top Model\' (2003-2018) Credit: The CW Starring: Tyra Banks , Janice Dickinson, Nigel Barker, Twiggy, Jay Manuel, J. Alexander Why it makes the list: If you aren’t wondering whatever happened to ANTM winners Adrianne Curry, Eva Marcille, or CariDee English every once in a blue moon, you probably didn’t come up in the 2000s. With its weekly photoshoots, go-see challenges, and mind-blowing/traumatic makeovers, each cycle of ANTM proved more memorable than the last. (Though nothing will ever top the moment Tyra lost her cool on a contestant and instantly became a time-honored meme .) WATCH NOW \'The City\' (2008–2010) Credit: Alamy/Wenn Rights Ltd. Starring: Whitney Port, Olivia Palermo, Erin Kaplan, Joe Zee, Kelly Cutrone, and Roxy Olin Why it makes the list: The City had all the drama we loved from The Hills and upped the fashion stakes. It follows Lauren’s former Teen Vogue co-intern, Whitney Port, as she embarks on a journey to become a respected fashion designer. If only she could get her frenemy Olivia Palermo from the Elle accessories department on board… WATCH NOW \'The Girls Next Door\' (2005–2010) Credit: Alamy Starring: Holly Madison, Bridget Marquardt, Kendra Wilkinson, and Hugh Hefner Why it makes the list: Love it or hate it, the Playboy Mansion and its female inhabitants became a cultural phenomenon in the mid-\'00s with the debut of the reality series The Girls Next Door . Rather than focusing on the mansion’s infamous owner, Hugh Hefner, the series shone a spotlight on the women who lived inside its walls: namely, Holly Madison, Bridget Marquardt, and Kendra Wilkinson. Madison later called it “ the most bizarre show that was ever on television ,” citing the family-friendly packaging of their taboo and highly sexualized reality, which she later detailed in a 2015 tell-all book . WATCH NOW \'The Hills\' (2006–2010) Credit: MTV Starring: Lauren Conrad, Kristin Cavallari, Audrina Patridge, Brody Jenner, Heidi Montag, Spencer Pratt, and Justin Bobby Why it makes the list: Released in 2006, The Hills was a natural progression for fans of Laguna Beach , who followed heroine Lauren Conrad’s move from her idyllic hometown to the big bad city. She got a whole lot more than a new zip code, including an internship at Teen Vogue , a new crush or two (ahem, Brody Jenner), and plenty of new fun-loving besties to help her navigate life in the Hollywood Hills. WATCH NOW \'Laguna Beach\' (2004–2006) Credit: Getty Images Starring: Lauren Conrad, Kristin Cavallari , Stephen Colletti, Lo Bosworth, and Talan Torriero Why it makes the list: Laguna Beach walked so that The Hills could run! We\'re forever thankful to MTV for following eight Laguna Beach teens during their last years of high school, creating high-quality entertainment (and a whole new vernacular—donezo, anyone?) in the process. WATCH NOW \'Punk\'d\' (2003–2015) Credit: MTV Starring: Ashton Kutcher Why it makes the list: Watching your favorite celebs get secretly pranked by other A-listers (its host was Ashton Kutcher) was peak reality television. How many of them kept cool during the high-stress situations is astounding. WATCH NOW \'Rock of Love with Bret Michaels\' (2007–2009) Credit: VH1 Starring: Brett Michaels Why it makes the list: Long before there was Love Island , there was Rock of Love —the raunchy, over-the-top dating show that gave glam metal groupies the chance to date Bret Michaels, a.k.a. the lead singer of Poison. If you’ve never seen this one, let’s say you’re in for a treat: These ladies make The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives crew look tame. WATCH NOW \'The Simple Life\' (2003–2007) Credit: Alamy Starring: Paris Hilton and Nicole Richie Why it makes the list: This "reality" series about two Hollywood socialites ditching their designer handbags and extravagant ways to live like "the middle class" is \'00s reality TV at its best. Our favorite line? "What is Walmart?" WATCH NOW The Best 2000s Teen Shows \'Dawson\'s Creek\' (1998–2003) Credit: Alamy Starring: James Van Der Beek, Katie Holmes , Michelle Williams, Joshua Jackson, and Busy Philipps Why it makes the list: The 2000s were the golden age of teen drama, and none led the charge quite like Dawson’s Creek . It follows the intertwined everyday dramas of Dawson Leery (Van Der Beek) and his closest friends throughout their high school (and early college) days in a small New England town while tackling a range of real-world issues such as classism, homophobia, and mental health. WATCH NOW \'Degrassi: The Next Generation\' (2001–2015) Credit: CTV Starring : Miriam McDonald, Shane Kippel, Cassie Steele, Lauren Collins, Stefan Brogren, and Drake Why it makes the list : Degrassi was the Canadian drama of the \'00s with its honest depictions of real-life problems affecting teens (bullying, teen pregnancy, school shootings) and its knockout cast that featured several generations of young stars. WATCH NOW \'Freaks and Geeks\' (1999–2000) Credit: Alamy Starring: Linda Cardellini, John Francis Daley, James Franco, Busy Philipps, Seth Rogen, and Jason Segel Why it makes the list: Unlike other canceled-too-soon shows on this list that were later revived or turned into feature films down the line, Freaks and Geeks remains a one-season wonder. But that hasn’t stopped the Judd Apatow-produced series from becoming a beloved cult classic, thanks to its spot-on depiction of high school’s often impossible-to-navigate social system. WATCH NOW \'Friday Night Lights\' (2006–2011) Credit: Alamy Starring: Kyle Chandler, Taylor Kitsch, Brad Leland, Connie Britton, Aimee Teegarden, and Zach Gilford Why it makes the list: Say it with us, "Clear eyes. Full hearts. Can\'t lose." While we can\'t technically attend a Dillon Panthers football game (ugh), Friday Night Lights was one of the strongest and most well-executed teen dramas of its time, tackling topics like racism and teen pregnancy through a whole new lens. WATCH NOW \'Gilmore Girls\' (2000–2007) Credit: Alamy Starring: Lauren Graham, Alexis Bledel, Milo Ventimiglia, Jared Padalecki, Scott Patterson, and Melissa McCarthy Why it makes the list: Forget Team Conrad or Team Jere: Back in the 2000s, it was Team Dean, Team Jess, or Team Logan. And we have Rory Gilmore and her crippling inability to make a proper decision on Gilmore Girls to thank for it. WATCH NOW \'Glee\' (2009–2015) Credit: Fox Starring: Chris Colfer, Jane Lynch, Lea Michele, Kevin McHale, Matthew Morrison, Naya Rivera, Corey Monteith, and Amber Riley Why it makes the list: Every theatre kid’s dream come true, Glee set high school antics to the soundtrack of the ‘00s, making it a time capsule of sorts for those who didn’t get to revel in all of the era’s adolescent glory firsthand. The guest appearances didn’t suck, either: everyone from Britney Spears and Gwyneth Paltrow to John Stamos and Sarah Jessica Parker made a cameo. WATCH NOW \'Gossip Girl\' (2008–2012) Credit: The CW Starring: Blake Lively , Leighton Meester , Penn Badgley, Taylor Momsen, Ed Westwick, and Chace Crawford Why it makes the list: What\'s better than watching a bunch of hot, wealthy New York socialites get in all sorts of messy drama while simultaneously trying to avoid becoming the wrath of Gossip Girl , a.k.a. the most life-ruining anonymous gossip blog, like, ever? Nothing, of course. This one also gets major bonus points for the weekly style inspo . WATCH NOW \'The O.C.\' (2003–2007) Credit: Fox Starring: Ben McKenzie, Mischa Barton , Adam Brody , Rachel Bilson , Peter Gallagher, and Kelly Rowan Why it makes the list: Fun fact: This teenage soap drama set in Southern California\'s Newport Beach was the inspiration for MTV\'s Laguna Beach . It also features a baby-faced Adam Brody trying to survive high school before he was making us all swoon on Nobody Wants This . WATCH NOW \'One Tree Hill\' (2003–2012) Credit: Collection Christophel Starring: Chad Michael Murray , James Lafferty, Hilarie Burton, Bethany Joy Lenz, Sophia Bush , and Lee Norris Why it makes the list: This high school drama set in Tree Hill, North Carolina can get a bit cheesy at times, but it\'s also a coming-of-age staple that paved the way for the Riverdale set, so we\'re going to go ahead and give credit where credit is due. WATCH NOW \'Popular\' (1999–2001) Credit: The WB Starring: Leslie Bibb, Carly Pope, Sara Rue, Tamara Mello, Leslie Grossman, Christopher Gorham, and Tammy Lynn Michaels Why it makes the list: There’s a reason Leslie Bibb rocked the cunty little bob so hard in White Lotus —it wasn’t her first rodeo. In the early 2000s, her Popular character Brooke McQueen had a similar cut to match her mean girl (eventually turned sweet) persona. More than just giving us her fabulous coif, however, this show was a harbinger of great teen drama to come as HBIC Brooke is forced to move in with the studious Sam McPherson (Pope) when their parents get engaged. \'Smallville (2001-2011) Credit: The WB Starring: Tom Welling, Allison Mack, Kristin Kreuk, Michael Rosenbaum, Erica Durance, Justin Hartley Why it makes the list: What if Superman grew up in small-town Kansas and had to deal with the trials and tribulations of everyday life as a teen before he learned how to harness his superpowers to save the world? Such is the plot of Smallville. It also gives some backstory to his early relationships with Lois Lane (Durance) and Lex Luthor (Rosenbaum). It seems people associated him with his Twilight character, Edward Cullen, a little too much until he skillfully moved away from the "cursed" Twilight lore and his controversial relationship with his Twilight co-star, Kristen Stewart . Instead, he made everyone swallow their words and became one of the best actors of today. Pattinson usually very evidently provides his own twist on characters , which is what makes him stand out; this took some time and bold choices, of course, but he\'s finally established himself as a master of his own fate in those respects. Whether he\'s using a silly voice, dyeing his hair, or taking on a thick, Southern accent , he\'s ready to transform and perform. If you’re interested, here are the best Robert Pattinson movies, according to IMDb rankings. 10 \'Water for Elephants\' (2011) IMDb Rating: 6.9/10 Jacob (Robert Pattinson) with an elephant in \'Water for Elephants\' Image via 20th Century Studios Water for Elephants may not have been the biggest hit of the 2010s, but it\'s a touching story about love , individuality, and freedom . Pattinson stars as the compassionate lead, a stand-up character you find yourself cheering for from the jump; he\'s joined by Reese Witherspoon as his love interest and Christoph Waltz as the cruel antagonist. No one particularly stands out, except the elephant, Tai , who is always the star of every scene and a beautiful, gentle giant. Water for Elephants follows Jacob (Pattinson), a runaway veterinary medicine student who joins the circus of famed ringmaster, August (Christoph Waltz), and begins to care for the animals. When August brings the elephant Rosie to the circus, he urges Jacob to train her, but August\'s mistreatment of the animal, his employees, and his own wife , Marlena (Reese Witherspoon), becomes too much for Jacob. Despite some critics saying there was a lack of chemistry between Witherspoon and Pattinson, their performances are great, and the movie is a great example of nice family fun full of familiar, talented faces. 9 \'Remember Me\' (2010) IMDb Rating: 7.1/10 Emilie de Ravin caressing Robert Pattinson\'s face in \'Remember Me\' Image via Summit Entertainment Remember Me is, honestly, much higher-rated than critics initially approved of. Many have considered its final twist to be tasteless , with some even using the word "offensive," but the movie takes an interesting, if not dramatic, perspective on just some of the events and lives that take place in NYC every single day. People are divided on this film, but Pattinson leads the movie as a handsome, brutish, rebellious rich kid with self-control issues ; he does it quite naturally, despite many interviews revealing Pattinson to be shy and sometimes awkward. Remember Me is a romantic drama about Tyler (Pattinson), the son of distant, workaholic Charles ( Pierce Brosnan ) and older brother to Caroline ( Ruby Jerins ). On the other hand, there\'s Ally ( Emilie de Ravin ), the rebellious daughter of NYPD detective Neil ( Chris Cooper ). A plan to take revenge bonds Tyler and Ally, and they fall in love despite how they met . In spite of some melodramatic twists and turns , Remember Me is a touching story that shows character development and growth. 8 \'The Devil All the Time\' (2020) IMDb Rating: 7.1/10 The Devil All the Time was one of those movies people watched and couldn\'t believe Pattinson\'s character choices, most notably his interpretation of a Southern accent ( for which he didn\'t use a coach ). Still, despite a majorly stellar cast, he was the one who earned the highest praise for capturing the movie\'s sinister tone with his performance and is its most memorable character. The Devil All the Time is a dark descent into depravity, depicting pretty much all the awful things that could happen within a span of two hours—though the story is dispersed throughout decades. The Devil All the Time is set in the small town of Knockemstiff, Ohio, and begins during WWII, continuing into 1950, 1957, and 1965. It follows various characters in town, focusing on Arvin ( Tom Holland ), whose inner battle with his family\'s demons interferes with his outward battle against the eccentric self-righteous preacher, Preston Teagarden (Pattinson). The story is narrated by Donald Ray Pollock, who is the author of the novel the movie was based on . Pattinson and Holland are two English actors who are thrilling as characters born and bred in the deep American South, and it\'s a joy to watch them step out of the usual mold they were put in as a glittery vampire and a Marvel superhero , respectively. 7 \'Good Time\' (2017) IMDb Rating: 7.3/10 Robert Pattinson walking down a hallway in Good Time Image via A24 Good Time is one of the first movies by the Safdie brothers , and one that propelled them into mainstream stardom. It showed us the scope of their work and their creative vision, but it also became one of the more defining movies in Pattinson\'s career . Good Time was potentially the first time people started to realize what a great, versatile actor he is . His character is responsible for his younger brother, but he himself is often in complete disarray; as with any Safdie film, this one is chaotic, intense, and vivid. Pattinson has terribly bleached hair in Good Time , but he also shows off a distinctive action star prowess. Good Time follows Connie (Pattinson) and his younger brother Nick ( Benny Safdie ), who run away after a botched robbery attempt. The escape plan doesn\'t work and Nick ends up on Rikers Island , so Connie must run around New York City to collect bail money before Nick gets hurt. Good Time is quite anxiety-inducing ; it has a lot of running, close calls, and plenty of seedy characters scattered across the NYC underbelly. With Pattinson\'s brilliant performance, we are compelled to feel his frustration and cheer for him, even though he keeps making wrong moves and gets bad cards dealt. 6 \'The King\' (2019) IMDb Rating: 7.3/10 Robert Pattinson as Louis, Duke of Guyenne in \'The King\' Image via Netflix The King stars Timothée Chalamet as the eponymous king , the young Henry V. The film was based on several of William Shakespeare \'s works involving King Henry, and it was written by Joel Edgerton , who also stars, and David Michod , who directed the film. It\'s an underrated historical epic , and it\'s quite dark and grimy. Chalamet is pretty solid and embodies a young king perfectly, but the star of the show is Pattinson as the French Dauphin, Louis. His French accent while speaking English, the sinister nasal laugh and the incessant burns against King Henry are scene-stealers through and through. The King follows the young Henry V, the son of the king who now goes by Hal and lives among the people. However, Hal is suddenly crowned as the new ruler and has to learn to embrace the royal life after spending years trying to ditch it all. The story is set in the 15th century and is a biographical drama; it was acted and filmed beautifully, and despite being a slow burn, it\'s quite captivating and commands attention from start to finish. If anything, it\'s fun when we get to see Pattinson hurl ridiculous insults at Chalamet—I mean, Louis at Hal. 5 \'Tenet\' (2020) IMDb Rating: 7.3/10 Robert Pattinson as Neil in Christopher Nolan\'s \'Tenet\' Image via Warner Bros. Tenet came at a time when culture and cultural events had to take a pause due to the pandemic, so there was a lot of enthusiasm for a new Christopher Nolan feature. However, the film turned out to be quite confusing, failing to win people over as much as anticipated . Pattinson is joined by John David Washington , and they make a pretty stellar team; although Washington is the protagonist, Pattinson is a crucial character for his success in the mission, and he plays a more polished and subdued character compared to some of his other work. Tenet follows a hero only known as The Protagonist (John David Washington), a CIA operative recruited by an organization called Tenet and sent on a global rescue mission ; Tenet assigns Neil (Pattinson) to be The Protagonist\'s handler. The themes include entropy and the relativity of time; there are many interesting concepts and premises , and it\'s one of those movies you either have to watch several times to understand or simply have to be a genius to get it immediately . Pattinson plays a calm and collected agent, so he didn\'t venture out into crazy and bizarre characteristics but kept the character classy and mysterious. 4 \'The Boy and the Heron\' (2023) IMDb Rating: 7.4/10 The grey heron watches Mahito from the water in The Boy and the Heron Image via Studio Ghibli Pattinson\'s rising career has also taken him to animated features, and voicing one of Hayao Miyazaki \'s films is a grand achievement of its own. 2023\'s biggest animated feature, The Boy and the Heron , is one of the best movies of the past decade; it\'s a classic Studio Ghibli masterpiece , hand-drawn and animated to perfection. Everything, from the colors to the voice acting, is incredible, and the English dubbing gathered some of Hollywood\'s biggest stars. Besides Pattinson, there are Florence Pugh , Christian Bale , Mark Hamill , and Willem Dafoe . The Boy and the Heron is set during the Pacific War and follows Mahito Maki, a teenage boy who moves with his father to a rural estate of his aunt, Natsuko, after his mother passes away. Near the estate, Mahito meets a peculiar Grey Heron, which leads him into a sealed tower that seems to be the final place his great-granduncle was seen. The heron seems malicious at first but is actually an ally to Mahito; Pattinson voices him and immerses his eccentric self fully. As he\'s apparently a fan of silly voices, Pattinson gives the heron a screechy, monstrous vocal and sounds unrecognizable . His contribution is one of the best parts of the already brilliant animation. 3 \'The Lighthouse\' (2019) IMDb Rating: 7.4/10 The Lighthouse is one of the greatest psychological thrillers/horrors of the past decade, largely due to the exceptional performances by Pattinson and Willem Dafoe . There\'s a lot that makes The Lighthouse beautiful, from vintage camerawork and a haunting musical score to the atmosphere, which greatly contributes to the choices of the actors and their performances . Since it\'s a movie about isolation and madness, it seems like there were hardly any better picks than Pattinson and Dafoe; both of them seem more than willing to take dramatic risks and embrace the bizarre and the unknown. The Lighthouse follows two lighthouse keepers, Ephraim (Pattinson) and Thomas (Willem Dafoe), beginning their four-week shift at the lighthouse on a remote New England island. Thomas is a former sailor and believes that seagulls are reincarnated sailors; after Ephraim kills one, strange and unnerving things begin to happen . Combine superstition with isolation, paranoia, and mythology, and Ephraim and Thomas begin to lose their minds. The Lighthouse is a stunning movie , but it may be difficult or even too artsy for some people; Pattinson\'s performance as Ephraim is hypnotic and only boosted by Dafoe\'s freedom of expression. Together, they\'re a hallucinatory pair, making The Lighthouse a must-watch. 2 \'Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire\' (2005) IMDb Rating: 7.7/10 Robert Pattinson as Cedric Diggory aims a wand at someone off-screen in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire. Image via Warner Bros. Interestingly enough, one of the highest-rated movies on Pattinson\'s IMDb page is Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire , a movie in which he\'s a side character. However, this is his breakout role, and his character Cedric Diggory was more or less essential for the success of the film . Pattinson\'s poster was on the walls of many teenagers\' rooms, showing a dressed-up Cedric sweetly smiling through the picture; we got to know Pattinson as a heartthrob, which was why he was hired to do Twilight. In a way, many of us are glad he broke the mold, but it\'s also worth remembering where he started . Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire is the fourth movie in the Harry Potter series. In the Goblet of Fire , Hogwarts is the host school of a Triwizard Tournament, in which they participate with the Durmstrang Institute and the Beauxbatons Academy. The magical Goblet of Fire chooses the champions for the tournament , and in Hogwarts, it picks both Cedric Diggory and Harry Potter ( Daniel Radcliffe ). While people believe Harry cheated his way into the tournament, Cedric becomes the favorite and a heartthrob. It’s very simple: if you like Harry Potter , then you probably like Pattinson; Goblet of Fire was big , and we must admit it was partly because of him. 1 \'The Batman\' (2022) IMDb Rating: 7.8/10 Robert Pattinson as the titular character in The Batman (2022), standing outside at sunrise or sunset while brooding Image via Warner Bros. Many found it controversial that Pattinson was chosen to be the next Batman /Bruce Wayne in The Batman . However, agree or disagree, he was a great choice, fully capable of portraying a brutish vigilante and a polished billionaire at the same time . So, when the seemingly innocent and sheltered Bruce Wayne steps into the costume of the confident and fearless Batman, he can only transform in attitude, and Pattinson has a way of embracing that without over-delivering or over-promising. The Batman is set in Gotham and follows the characters of the city\'s dark underbelly, introducing audiences to its most notorious and fiercest. The Riddler ( Paul Dano ) terrorizes the city with calculated bomb attacks, and Batman chases after him; at the same time, Oswald "The Penguin" Cobb ( Colin Farrell ) plots his way out from under Carmine Falcone\'s wings. The Batman is, surprisingly and satisfyingly, a visually gorgeous homage to noir films and thrillers ; it transcends the superhero limitations and turns into a universally watchable and adored crime flick. Pattinson will return as The Caped Crusader in Matt Reeves\' highly anticipated sequel , and we\'re kind of excited to see him in another brilliant outing. Dan Clarendon, TV Insider Nov 8, 2025 Nov 8, 2025 Updated Nov 8, 2025 Comments Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save When Lost didn’t have us scratching our heads , it had us dabbing our eyes. For as much as the ABC castaway drama constructed a mysterious and metaphysical mythology that we’re still trying to wrap our minds around , it also moved us with human drama anyone can understand. This is a show that yanked at our heart strings, often while we heard a swell of strings. (Damn that Michael Giacchino and his emotional orchestrations!) Here’s a (very spoilery) rundown of the moments that had us emotionally lost… 9. Claire apologizes to her mother Not only does a Season 3 episode show Claire ( Emilie de Ravin ) meeting her father — who’s Jack’s ( Matthew Fox ) father, too! — it also shows her sobbing as she says goodbye to her mother. Carole (Susan Duerden) was in a coma ever after getting into a car crash with Claire years earlier, and Claire tearfully confesses her past sins before taking her ill-fated flight to Los Angeles. “I’m so sorry for all the awful things I said to you in the car — that I hated you, and that I wished you weren’t my mother, and I wished you were dead,” Claire says. “It’s all my fault, the accident and everything.” 8. Kate says goodbye to Aaron After Claire disappears into the jungle in Season 4, the other survivors care for her baby son, Aaron. He’s one of the so-called Oceanic Six who make it back to civilization that season, and Kate ( Evangeline Lilly ) raises him as her own for years. But when Kate realizes she has to go back to the Island to rescue Claire, she leaves Aaron with Claire’s (then-recovered) mother, tears streaming down her face as she bids the little guy farewell. 7. Locke’s father betrays him In one of many chapters of Locke’s ( Terry O’Quinn ) tragic life, we see the rise and fall of his relationship with his biological father via Season 1 flashbacks. Locke locates the long-lost Cooper ( Kevin Tighe ), and they seemingly recapture their father-son relationship. Locke even donates a kidney to his dad when he discovers Cooper is in kidney failure. But Cooper is a con man, and when he takes the organ and runs, Locke is left devastated. 6. Vincent makes sure Jack doesn’t die alone Lost ends the series finale as the series premiere started, with Jack walking through the Island’s bamboo forest and spotting Vincent, the yellow Labrador that also survived the crash of Oceanic 815. But this time, Jack is dying, and as he collapses to the leafy ground, Vincent lies down next to him. (“Live together, die alone”? Not if this good boy has anything to say about it.) And as one version of Jack perishes — and the flash-sideways version of him moves on to the afterlife with his Oceanic 815 buddies — he sees the Ajira plane pass overhead, carrying his surviving friends to safety. 5. Alex becomes a casualty of Ben’s negotiations with Keamy Ben ( Michael Emerson ) refuses to surrender to the mercenaries in Season 4, even when Keamy ( Kevin Durand ) reveals he has taken Alex, Ben’s adoptive daughter, hostage. Over Keamy’s walkie-talkie, Alex ( Tania Raymonde ) pleads for her life and begs Ben to give himself up, but Ben insists he has the situation under control. He doesn’t, of course — Keamy makes good on this threat and shoots Alex in the head, and the last thing the poor girl heard in her life was Ben claiming, untruthfully, that she means nothing to him. 4. Boone dies as Aaron is born The Island giveth and the Island taketh away. Claire gives birth to Aaron the same night that Boone ( Ian Somerhalder ), a fellow Oceanic 815 survivor, dies from injuries he sustained helping Locke investigate the wreckage of another crashed plane. And as the rest of the survivors crowd around Claire and her newborn, Shannon ( Maggie Grace ) heads to the cave and weeps over the body of her dead brother. 3. Sawyer tries in vain to save Juliet In Lost ’s Season 5 finale, our 1977-stranded heroes make a plan to send a hydrogen bomb down a drilling shaft at the site of the DHARMA Initiative’s Swan station — future home of The Hatch — in hopes of preventing the electromagnetic anomaly and thus the future crash of Oceanic 815. But Juliet ( Elizabeth Mitchell ) is pulled down into the shaft, and though she’s mortally wounded in that fall, Sawyer ( Josh Holloway ) still thinks he can save her after the bomb detonation sends them to 2007. She dies in his arms, telling him they can get coffee sometime (foreshadowing their flash-sideways reunion). 2. Charlie dies a hero’s death Desmond ( Henry Ian Cusick ) has visions of Charlie ( Dominic Monaghan ) dying throughout Season 3, but those premonitions don’t make the Drive Shaft musician’s demise any less tragic. Charlie drowns after Mikhail ( Andrew Divoff ) detonates a grenade outside the underwater Looking Glass station’s porthole — but not before making contact with Penny ( Sonya Walger ) and realizing the mercenaries on the freighter aren’t who they say they are. In his final moments, Charlie saves not just Desmond but many more of his friends, writing “NOT PENNY’S BOAT” on his palm as a dying warning. 1. Jin stays with Sun until the end Near the end of Season 6, the Man in Black plants a bomb on the submarine the survivors plan to use to escape the Island. Sayid ( Naveen Andrews ) sacrifices himself to save his friends — which is sad enough already! — but then Jin ( Daniel Dae Kim ) realizes Sun ( Yunjin Kim ) is pinned in the sinking sub. Dan Clarendon, TV Insider Nov 8, 2025 Nov 8, 2025 Updated Nov 8, 2025 Comments Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save When Lost didn’t have us scratching our heads , it had us dabbing our eyes. For as much as the ABC castaway drama constructed a mysterious and metaphysical mythology that we’re still trying to wrap our minds around , it also moved us with human drama anyone can understand. This is a show that yanked at our heart strings, often while we heard a swell of strings. (Damn that Michael Giacchino and his emotional orchestrations!) Here’s a (very spoilery) rundown of the moments that had us emotionally lost… 9. Claire apologizes to her mother Not only does a Season 3 episode show Claire ( Emilie de Ravin ) meeting her father — who’s Jack’s ( Matthew Fox ) father, too! — it also shows her sobbing as she says goodbye to her mother. Carole (Susan Duerden) was in a coma ever after getting into a car crash with Claire years earlier, and Claire tearfully confesses her past sins before taking her ill-fated flight to Los Angeles. “I’m so sorry for all the awful things I said to you in the car — that I hated you, and that I wished you weren’t my mother, and I wished you were dead,” Claire says. “It’s all my fault, the accident and everything.” 8. Kate says goodbye to Aaron After Claire disappears into the jungle in Season 4, the other survivors care for her baby son, Aaron. He’s one of the so-called Oceanic Six who make it back to civilization that season, and Kate ( Evangeline Lilly ) raises him as her own for years. But when Kate realizes she has to go back to the Island to rescue Claire, she leaves Aaron with Claire’s (then-recovered) mother, tears streaming down her face as she bids the little guy farewell. 7. Locke’s father betrays him In one of many chapters of Locke’s ( Terry O’Quinn ) tragic life, we see the rise and fall of his relationship with his biological father via Season 1 flashbacks. Locke locates the long-lost Cooper ( Kevin Tighe ), and they seemingly recapture their father-son relationship. Locke even donates a kidney to his dad when he discovers Cooper is in kidney failure. But Cooper is a con man, and when he takes the organ and runs, Locke is left devastated. 6. Vincent makes sure Jack doesn’t die alone Lost ends the series finale as the series premiere started, with Jack walking through the Island’s bamboo forest and spotting Vincent, the yellow Labrador that also survived the crash of Oceanic 815. But this time, Jack is dying, and as he collapses to the leafy ground, Vincent lies down next to him. (“Live together, die alone”? Not if this good boy has anything to say about it.) And as one version of Jack perishes — and the flash-sideways version of him moves on to the afterlife with his Oceanic 815 buddies — he sees the Ajira plane pass overhead, carrying his surviving friends to safety. 5. Alex becomes a casualty of Ben’s negotiations with Keamy Ben ( Michael Emerson ) refuses to surrender to the mercenaries in Season 4, even when Keamy ( Kevin Durand ) reveals he has taken Alex, Ben’s adoptive daughter, hostage. Over Keamy’s walkie-talkie, Alex ( Tania Raymonde ) pleads for her life and begs Ben to give himself up, but Ben insists he has the situation under control. He doesn’t, of course — Keamy makes good on this threat and shoots Alex in the head, and the last thing the poor girl heard in her life was Ben claiming, untruthfully, that she means nothing to him. Boone dies as Aaron is born The Island giveth and the Island taketh away. Claire gives birth to Aaron the same night that Boone ( Ian Somerhalder ), a fellow Oceanic 815 survivor, dies from injuries he sustained helping Locke investigate the wreckage of another crashed plane. And as the rest of the survivors crowd around Claire and her newborn, Shannon ( Maggie Grace ) heads to the cave and weeps over the body of her dead brother. 3. Sawyer tries in vain to save Juliet In Lost ’s Season 5 finale, our 1977-stranded heroes make a plan to send a hydrogen bomb down a drilling shaft at the site of the DHARMA Initiative’s Swan station — future home of The Hatch — in hopes of preventing the electromagnetic anomaly and thus the future crash of Oceanic 815. But Juliet ( Elizabeth Mitchell ) is pulled down into the shaft, and though she’s mortally wounded in that fall, Sawyer ( Josh Holloway ) still thinks he can save her after the bomb detonation sends them to 2007. The Duchess of Sussex , 44, is said to have been 'swamped with offers' for her return to the limelight, and will be playing herself in the film Close Personal Friends, with filming taking place in Pasadena in LA. But before she married Prince Harry and joined the royal family , Meghan's acting career looked very different - consisting mainly of bit parts and cameos in largely forgettable and poorly reviewed movies - and she was not nearly so in demand. Before making her name as Rachel Zane in the TV show Suits, Meghan secured minor Hollywood roles in Horrible Bosses (2011) and Remember Me (2010) - where she was typecast as a 'cute' or 'hot girl', with only seconds of screentime . Often, her cameo and pilot roles, such as her brief appearance kissing Russell Brand in Get Him To The Greek (2010) and The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down (2011), never actually ended up making the final cut. As a result, the now-Duchess was forced to resort to a series of raunchy roles - and was seen parading around in sexy negligee for the majority of her feature in 2012's Random Encounters - not to mention her explicit scene in the 90210 TV series . Critics, meanwhile, were less than impressed with the final results, even warning viewers that Meghan's 2006 film Deceit would 'bore them to death'. When she finally did score leading roles towards the end of her acting career, Meghan was mainly seen in repetitive and unchallenging Hallmark Movies, receiving mixed reviews at best. The mother-of-two previously told how she would get plenty of auditions but was regularly rejected by directors - which was a 'lot to chip away at your self-esteem'. Here, we give a rundown of all Meghan's film roles before meeting Prince Harry - most of which you probably won't have heard of... A Lot Like Love (2005) Meghan made her film debut in 2005, playing Natalie, the 'Hot Girl' in A Lot Like Love Meghan, then aged 24 and an unknown actress, made her big screen debut alongside Hollywood heartthrob Ashton Kutcher in the 2005 film called A Lot Like Love , where she was famously credited as 'Hot Girl.' The Duchess' very first film role was a total flop at the box office but Meghan herself, wearing a bright pink top, was only on screen for 31 seconds, and saw her attempting to flirt with Kutcher's internet entrepreneur character Oliver Martin on a flight. But she was left stunned when Oliver showed no interest because of his complicated on-off relationship with photographer Emily Friehl, Alias actress Amanda Peet. And she ended up being chatted up by business partner Jetter played by actor Kal Penn instead, who was sat across the aisle. Although she introduced herself as Natalie, she only appeared in the credits as 'Hot Girl.' The film was like an American version of One Day, where a couple met regularly over a seven-year period before falling in love. The moment was featured in Harry and Meghan's Netflix docu-series as they discussed Meghan's film career. The film received mixed reviews and a score of 40 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes, while one review in the Observer called it 'neither bad nor good enough to be anything other than utterly forgettable'. Deceit (2006) Meghan played Gwen in 2006's Deceit, again another small role for the budding actress In her second film role, Meghan again landed only a small part, playing a girl-next-door called Gwen, again appearing only in one scene. Over the kitchen table, Meghan's characeter dispensed unwanted advice to a friend caught up in a murder mystery. Her handy advice included lines such as: 'You're an investigative journalist; do what you do best - investigate her' The psychological thriller, released in 2006, followed a young man returning home after his father's death and falling in love with his best friend's wife. It explored attraction, violence, and deception. Meghan played Gwen in one scene in the film, a friend of the protagonist who offered advice to the main character. Director Matthew Cole Weiss previously revealed he'd met Prince Harry, who told him he had watched the film. The film has poor reviews online, scoring just 4.5/10 on IMDB, with viewers saying it has 'weak acting,' 'no characters' adding it will 'bore you to death'. Remember Me (2010) The Duchess did score some Hollywood roles in her film acting career, starring in Remember Me alongside Robert Pattinson In Remember Me, starring Robert Pattinson and Emilie de Ravin, Meghan had a small role as a bartender, who was aptly named Megan. She briefly interacted with Pattinson's character and only had one, three-word line: 'Do not speak', when she told his friend not to chat with her. On working with the Twilight star, Meghan recalled: 'He's a really lovely guy and a really great example to be able to watch someone who is young, who's stardom has really taken over his live in such a huge way, and yet he's still gracious, humble and cool. I think that is really endearing.' This movie marked Robert Pattinson's departure from his Twilight fame, so it would be easy to forget that a future star had a small role in the same production as well. The movie follows the story of Tyler Hawkins, who falls in love with Amy, played by Emilie de Ravin, but dies in the Twin Towers on 9/11/2001. The rom com was a financial success, grossing $56million worldwide. However, it fared less well with critics, only scoring 26 per cent on Rotten Tomatoes. The twist at the end of the show - that Pattinson's character is in his father's office in the World Trade Centre when the 9/11 attacks take place - was branded 'shockingly offensive' by Rolling Stone, and 'exploitative' by other reviewers. Meghan's real life ex-husband Trevor Engelson, was one of the film's producers, and the pair tied the knot a year later, during a party-filled celebration in Jamaica in 2011. They eventually divorced in 2014, with Meghan being linked to several men during her single years before she met now-husband Prince Harry in 2016. Get Him To The Greek (2010) Meghan Markle played Tatiana in comedy Get Him To The Greek, in which she's seen kissing comedian Russell Brand Meghan Markle played Tatiana in comedy Get Him To The Greek, in which she's seen kissing comedian Russell Brand. She reportedly had a 40-second role as a girl in a strapless metallic dress and snogged Brand's character. However, Meghan was never given a credit in the film and the scene never made it to the final cut. Is this really her? Everyone, including royal biographer Andrew Morton, says yes, reported the Mail's Jan Moir . The plot followed a record company employee, played by Jonah Hill, who went to London to get an eccentric English rock star (Russell Brand) to the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles. However, Snow is a party animal and took them on a wild ride involving alcohol and women, meeting Meghan Markle along the way. Speaking to the Evening Standard, Russell Brand said: 'She [Meghan] was in a film that I did, Get Him To The Greek it was called. 'I don't remember the film that much but I think I planted one on her. Scripted in the scene. I only know this because I think I saw a clip of it somewhere. 'They should bring that up [at the wedding]... if anyone has any reason... yeah Russell Brand snogged her in the film!' He said he didn't realise she was in it at the time as she 'wasn't married to a royal person'. The film was not panned by critics and was even said to have had its 'moments' - though Meghan's role was too short to appear in any of them. Horrible Bosses (2011) Horrible Bosses continued the trend of Meghan playing bit parts in Hollywood dark comedies Horrible Bosses in 2011 saw Meghan star alongside Jennifer Aniston and Jason Sudeikis. However, it seemed to continue the trend of her playing bit parts in Hollywood dark comedies, again having only a short cameo. The movie told the story of three employees who conspired to kill their overbearing employers. Meghan played courier driver Jamie in the comedy film and shared a few lines with Sudeikis' Kurt Buckman in another 30-second scene. In her scene, Jason Sudeikis chatted her up, saying: 'You're too cute to be a FedEx girl. You've got to be an actress or a model or something.' Her small role in the movie resurfaced after her relationship with Prince Harry became public. The film was surprisingly successful, but Meghan's role didn't attract any noticeable attention at the time. The Boys and Girls Guide to Getting Down (2011) Meghan Markle played Dana in the pilot to The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down, which never went anywhere Meghan Markle played Dana in The Boys And Girls Guide To Getting Down, which followed a group of friends on a night out in Los Angeles. The movie is described in the trailer as 'a film about sex drugs, booze and all around bad behaviour.' Filmed in 2011, and directed by Michael Shapiro, Meghan's character worked as a guide to Californian party-lovers, advising them on what to do and what not to do on a night out. The tongue-in-cheek movie touched on a lot of raunchy subjects, including drugs, sex and alcohol. Meghan's character Dana was seen snorting cocaine, wearing a tight black dress and obsessing about getting a boob job. The TV movie, described as a 'real life guide to sexy, drugs, and bad behavior', was filmed prior to Meghan landing her role on Suits and never went anywhere. According to IMDB, the pilot 'takes you through a night of partying in L.A.' It is described as 'funny' and 'somewhat outrageous' while offering advice to viewers on the ins and outs of partying. '[The film] gives partiers helpful tips about which substances should not be mixed, how to approach potential hook-ups, avoid undesirables [and] basically have a good time without completely destroying yourself,' the plot read on IMDB. The Candidate (2011) The Candidate, 2011: Meghan pulls strings to get a role in this hard-boiled sci-fi short film — which was produced by her then-husband, Trevor Engelson Sci-fi short film The Candidate (2011) was also produced by Meghan's then-husband, Trevor Engelson. The role was again a brief one, with Meghan starring in two scenes as Kat the secretary whose boss, Burton Grunzer, wanted to kill his incompetent colleague, Whitman Hayes. Meghan's character read her boss a latter from someone called Carl Tucker, whose text messages he repeatedly ignored. The film, by David Karlak, itself is only 19 minutes long, but received a positive reaction at the time, with one person saying it was 'better than most thrillers I've seen in theaters'. A description on the American Film Institute website reads: 'An underhanded company man is offered assistance by a secret organization that immerses him in forces beyond his control.' Dysfunctional Friends (2012) Meghan played photographer Terry in 2012's low budget film, 'Dysfunctional Friends' In the low budget film 'Dysfunctional Friends', Meghan showed she also has experience on the other side of the camera. Playing glamorous photographer Terry, Markle was seen in the little-known film shooting a handsome underwear model in a scene in scene focusing on his manhood. With flowing locks and wearing a black vest with off-the-shoulder baggy shirt, a no-nonsense Terry told male model Stylz, played by Christian Keyes: 'This is not porn. It's for the Sunday papers. This situation you have going on, it's got to get tucked in.' The images, for an underwear campaign, saw Markle's character getting increasingly frustrated with how her model was sat, before finally raging at him: 'Tuck it in!' The film followed nine friends who went their different ways after finishing college before reuniting at a rich friend's funeral. They find out that they will be eligible for a big inheritance if they stay at his mansion for five days. It bombed at the box office but paved the way for Markle to take on more serious roles. Keyes later told People Magazine that he had been 'slapped' by the 'future Queen' during filming. He explained: '[Meghan] said, 'I might improv an extra smack,' and I was like, 'smack away!' 'I knew she was going to put a little hand on it. She had some torque and rotation in the wrist.' 'It was one of her first acting gigs and she has [acting] chops, she had them back then. She was great on set. She was super cool and approachable. She was a class act.' Random Encounters (2013) Meghan had another racy role in Random Encounters, playing party girl Mindy Filmed over 18 days in 2010, the low budget romantic comedy was set in the showbusiness community in Los Angeles In Random Encounters, Meghan played Mindy, a party girl who brings home a different guy every night, and the best friend of singleton Laura, who strikes up a romance with Kevin, a man she met in a coffee shop. Filmed over 18 days in 2010, the low budget romantic comedy was set in the showbusiness community in Los Angeles. During the chick flick, which was made pre-Suits before being re-released, Mindy popped up in a host of revealing outfits including a sexy negligee before seducing a male co-star and sleeping with a cop who stopped her for a traffic offence. In one scene, Mindy could be seen showing her friend the ropes on 'the biggest dating site in LA'. She also revealed her top tips for catching a man's eye in a night club: 'Look like you're really bored and have a serious attitude problem.' When her frustrated single friend moaned that she is 'chasing a guy who doesn't insist,' Mindy replied: 'Oh honey, aren't we all.' 'It just goes to show, you just have to be in the right place at the right time. Sometimes, you only get one shot.' In one particularly racy scene Meghan was seen undressing actor Michael Rady as her character tried to make a move in a dimly-lit apartment. At other points in the film, Meghan flitted across the screen in flirty summer dresses and party frocks. Director Boris Undorf later spoke about Markle's can-do attitude while filming, reflecting: 'All the comforts of a bigger project weren't there. 'She was very much like, 'Yep, I got it. I know it's long hours, but I love doing it, and I'll do my best' to serve the film, not just myself.'' Co-star Abby Wathen (Laura) added: 'It was great to work with Meghan because she's a pro, and it's great to work with pros... It was lovely. We sat in my trailer and just giggled. She's just vivacious.' In 2018, the budget rom com was released in the UK for the first time - just two weeks before Meghan married Prince Harry. When Sparks Fly (2014) In 2014, Meghan finally landed her first major film role in Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly Meghan's character Amy finds there's no place like how when she reunited with her high school sweetheart In 2014, Meghan finally landed a major film role, playing the lead role in the Hallmark movie, When Sparks Fly. She played Amy Peterson, a journalist who quits her small town for the big city of Chicago. She then returned to her hometown to write a human interest story about Independence Day weekend. Amy discovered that there's no place like home - and no boy like her high school sweetheart. Meghan said at the time: 'I wanted to do a romantic comedy. When the script came in, it was exactly the kind of project I wanted to be part of. 'It was light and easy and it was a departure from Rachel [Suits], who is so refined and polished. Amy Peterson is very opposite and closer to my true personality. 'It was fun to eat ribs and get barbecue sauce all over my face and run around in jeans all day.' Hallmark films all generally follow the same plot points, and while they make for comforting watching, are generally not considered 'challenging' acting roles. In 2021 alone, the channel made 41 Christmas films, with each film relatively low budget and without famous names. Anti-Social (2015) Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin) in Anti-Social Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role Set in England and filmed largely in Hungary, Anti-Social followed a successful street artist who was forced to jeopardise his future to help his criminal brother when gang rivalry escalates. The gangland war turned their lives upside down, bringing the attention of the police as well as other criminals. The low-budget British coming-of-age story was inspired by a number of real-life smash-and-grab raids across London from 2009 to 2013. Again, the Duchess was chosen to play the female lead and it even co-starred grime star Skepta. Meghan - then 35 - played American fashion model Kirsten who falls in love with Dee (Gregg Sulkin), a talented Banksy-esque street-artist who was sucked into crime. One of her lines included: 'I know you have had to climb a mountain to get away from this crap and see life for what it can be. You inspire me.' Following her relationship with Prince Harry, the film was re-released and re-edited to give Meghan a bigger role as bosses sought to capitalise on her new royal links. Originally, it had been shown at just 40 screens in the UK when it was released in 2015. Speaking of the decision to re-release it, Director Reg Traviss - who had dated Amy Winehouse before she died - said he wanted to 'delve deeper into one of the storylines with.. a shorter, more compact version of the original'. In the three-minute trailer, Meghan's character was shown modelling perfume, emerging from a shower and drinking champagne at a number of West End nightclubs. She was heard saying: 'I'm going to go and see my boyfriend, he's an artist. A street artist.' In a scene which showed shoot-outs in London, depicting Marcus and his cool friends getting pulled into a dangerous gang war, she said: 'I hate violence... I'm from a sleepy little beach town, I'm just not used to this.' Upon its release, the film generally received negative reviews, with one critic calling the film a 'painful slog'. In The Observer, critic Mark Kermode awarded it two stars, calling it an 'uninspiring crime caper' that 'sits awkwardly alongside dreary discussions of the politics of street art'. Dater's Handbook (2016) Meghan's final film role saw her play Cassandra Barber in 2016's Dater's Handbook Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams In Meghan's final film role before quitting the industry upon joining the Royal Family, she played another lead role for the Hallmark Channel, in 2016's Dater's Handbook. The romantic movie centred around Cassandra Barber, who realised she had a recurring habit of picking the wrong type of guy, turning to relationship expert, Dr. Susie, and her latest self-help book, The Dater's Handbook to help with her ailing love life. 'Of course I wanna get married,' Meghan's character Cass told her mother. 'I've got to change how I choose relationships.' She followed the advice in Dr. Susie's book to evaluate potential suitors, and was forced to choose between reliable George (Jonathan Scarfe) and fun-loving Robert (Kristoffer Polaha). Cass soon realised that there was no rule book to love, binned her manual and met the man of her dreams. Little did Meghan know that six months later she'd meet her real-life prince. Successful career women, both Cassandra and Meghan were set up with their dream suitor by a mutual pal, bonding on and off-screen with their respective suitors over their shared love of animals and the great outdoors. Additionally, Meghan and her character were whisked away on sporty dates by their suitors - while Cass' mother joined the pair at a concert in the movie, Harry flew Meghan's mother Doria to the Invictus Games in Toronto in real life. Many joked at the time of the movie's release that while the character she played on screen had been unlucky in love, Meghan's real love life was very different. During the film's press tour, Meghan said: 'At the end of the day, when it comes down to finding the person that you're right for, that's not the person you're going to play games with. 'I think following her heart has really ended up proving to work out well for Cass, and I think for a lot of women watching this, I would give them that same advice.' The film, a classic Hallmark movie, was branded 'predictable and simple' by critics. On IMDB, one reviewer even said: 'The story was silly, the acting was below average, and the actors had no chemistry.'
